title: Unbiasing through Textual Descriptions: Mitigating Representation Bias in Video Benchmarks

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting specific concepts (e.g., only objects, only activities, or only verbs) from video frames using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs), and measuring if zero-shot models or linear classifiers can correctly predict the video label based solely on those isolated textual concepts.

Comparing video classification and retrieval performance when using textual representations of single frames (e.g., middle-frame, max-score frame) versus aggregated multi-frame temporal representations (e.g., sequence-of-frames, average-over-frames) to assess if true temporal reasoning is required.

bias_targets.target: Dataset bias vs. Common sense bias
bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the predictive performance of zero-shot text embedding models (which rely on pre-trained common sense knowledge) against linear logistic regression models trained on the specific dataset's training split (which exploit spurious, dataset-specific correlations).
